title: The checked-fields operation and payload on the treatment side, the treatment columns that carry the contract and mortgage facts, the masking of the treatment read and who stamps the type-table version are not specified
source: Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5, RWB E2 025 Extraction for the stage 2 and 3 document types v1, sections 11, 12, 13 and 16; Recovery Workbench TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2, T3.1, T3.2 and T-A.1; Recovery Workbench FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3, A2.1 and A2.18; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1, slides 16, 18 and 41; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1, sections R5.5 and R7.2
description: Legacy RWB-E2-025 gives the treatment side two things only: the in-process call DocumentFieldReader.checkedFields(UUID caseId, String documentType) returning List<CheckedField>, and the sentence that S2 reads confirmed field values through it to fill the treatment record. No source names the operation and the payload of the checked-fields read once it crosses the service boundary, and none gives the element names of the applied and withheld sets this story answers with. No source says which treatment column carries contract_amount, contract_date or the mortgage registration facts: TSD S2 T3.1 lists DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-033 and holds no contract and no mortgage field, so the fact columns are this story's design. No source says which role may see an unmasked party name on the treatment read: the legacy note limits unmasked values to a module whose purpose needs them and names SY-CASEWF and SY-AGENT, and rwb-treatment is named by neither. No source says who stamps the type-table version of the fields applied, whether rwb-document stamps it on its answer or the consumer stamps its own row. The story therefore records the operation name and payload as the baseline's, adds six fact columns and three source columns to treatment, keeps the masking of party_names with the hub, and stamps the tableVersion of the answer it wrote from on the row it writes.
evidence: Legacy section 12 publishes only List<CheckedField> checkedFields(UUID caseId, String documentType) with the comment 'CheckedField: documentId, docVersion, fieldName, value, state (OK, CONFIRMED, CORRECTED), confidence' and adds that values are returned unmasked only to a module whose purpose needs them (SY-CASEWF, SY-AGENT). Legacy section 13 adds no table and no column on the treatment side and names only DocumentFieldReader, DocumentFieldReaderImpl and DocumentFieldRepository. TSD S2 T3.1 lists treatment fields DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-033 with no contract amount, contract date, mortgage amount, registration date, land office or title document number. TSD S2 T-A.1 lists API-S2-001 to API-S2-004 only. Architecture v5 slide 18 gives rwb-treatment GET/POST /treatments and POST /treatments/{id}/offer with the topic rwb.treatment.events.v1, and slide 41 gives it treatments, contracts, settlement and deed-in-lieu agreements and plan timers with no field list.
area: Contract, data and masking design of the treatment-side document-fact fill
owner_role: Solution architect with the rwb-treatment and rwb-document squads
proposed: Take the operation, its path and its payload from RWB-P5-E2025-CON as published; add contract_amount, contract_date, mortgage_amount, registration_date, land_office and title_doc_no to treatment on the service Flyway sequence with the numeric(18,2) and date conventions TSD S2 T3.1 already uses, plus source_document_id, source_doc_version and source_table_version; keep party_names masked and stored nowhere; stamp the tableVersion of the reader's answer on the row in the same transaction as the facts.

title: Architecture v5 puts the S2 call to P5 in the Temporal column while the legacy published interface and DP-11 make the checked-fields read one REST hop
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1, slide 13 (connection matrix) and slides 18 and 20; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1, section R5.5 DP-11 and section R3 precedence; Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5, RWB E2 025 Extraction for the stage 2 and 3 document types v1, section 12; work package B-S2-06 story line for RWB-S2-E2025-APP
description: Two sources give the same read two transports. Architecture v5 slide 13 is the full connection matrix and puts the S2 Treatment row against the P5 Document column in the T cell, which is a Temporal activity on the owner's queue; its notes add that route services reach shared capabilities through Temporal and never through REST, and slide 12 says a step in another service is a Temporal activity while REST answers a person at the screen. The legacy story publishes the same read as an in-process interface that returns a value to its caller in the same request, and DP-11 turns an in-process published interface into a REST contract with a mock, one hop and a 2 s timeout; the work package names DP-11 in the pattern set and describes the call as a single REST call on one hop. By the precedence of R3 the architecture catalogue wins, but the architecture gives P5 no activity contract for a checked-field read, so following it would leave this story with no contract to build against on Day 1.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 13 row 'S2 Treatment' lists 'T' in the P5 Document column, and its notes read 'Route services reach shared capabilities through Temporal, never through REST'. Slide 12 lays out Q1 to Q4 and assigns a step in another service to Temporal. Slide 16 gives rwb-document the IN set POST /documents, GET /documents/{id}, GET /cases/{id}/documents, POST /documents/generate, the events AgentRunCompleted and the DocumentIntakeWorkflow, and no checked-field read at all; slide 18 gives rwb-treatment the OUT set Decision: child approval, Document: contract and e-sign, Payment: postProceeds and the ACE restructure calculator by Nexus, again with no checked-field read. Legacy RWB-E2-025 section 12 publishes DocumentFieldReader as a Java interface and section 9 calls it from the reading module in the same step. Template and Rules DP-11 reads 'REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout'.
area: Call type between rwb-treatment and rwb-document for the checked-field read
owner_role: Solution architect with the platform workflow team, rwb-document and rwb-treatment
proposed: Consume the checked-fields read as the published REST contract of RWB-P5-E2025-CON on one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker, as DP-11 and the work package give it, and build against its fake on Day 1; if the architecture review keeps the Temporal column, the read becomes a typed activity on queue rwb-document with the same payload and the same state filter, and this story's criteria, filter, mapper and writer are unchanged.

title: The treatment-side generation call, its two columns, the merge-field set and the generation event are not specified
source: RWB-E2-026 v1; TSD S2 T3.1 and T-A; FSD S2 v3 A2.18; Architecture v5 slides 18, 41 and 42; RWB-P5-E2026-CON
description: No source states the operation identifier of the generation call as rwb-treatment consumes it, the shape of the S2 merge-value set on the wire, which treatment columns hold the document reference and the pinned template version, the merge-field set of DIL-CONTRACT, DIL-CA, DIL-MORTGAGE and RES-AGREEMENT against the treatment columns, or the name, payload and decision code of the event a generation writes.
evidence: TSD S2 T3.1 lists DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-033 with no document-reference column and no template-version column; RWB-E2-026 section 12 names DocumentGenerator.generate as an in-process interface and no REST operation; RWB-E2-026 section 13 adds template_code, template_version and treatment_id to document and none to treatment; RWB-E2-026 section 7 names the merge fields of DIL-CONTRACT v2 as case_no, borrower_name, title_doc_no, transfer_price and contract_date and no treatment column carries contract_date; Architecture v5 slide 18 gives rwb-treatment the events TreatmentApproved and TreatmentClosed only.
proposed: Take the operation and its shapes from RWB-P5-E2026-CON, add the two nullable treatment columns and their index, supply only the values the treatment row holds, and keep the event name and code as this story's design until the event catalogue owner confirms them.

title: The template catalogue and merge fields sit with the document module in the legacy and with rwb-comms in the target
source: RWB-E2-026 v1; Architecture v5 slide 41; Ownership Map v1
description: The legacy files the template and merge-field catalogue under the document module's feature FEAT-OCC-07 with RWB-E1-046 and has the generation engine read it in process; Architecture v5 slide 41 and the Ownership Map give template and merge_field to P6 rwb-comms in rwb_comms. The legacy placement is the loser and this slice reads neither table.
evidence: RWB-E2-026 section 3 names RWB-E1-046 template and merge field catalog as data and section 12 declares TemplateCatalog.current and TemplateCatalog.mergeFields as interfaces the engine calls; Architecture v5 slide 41 row P6 reads 'notices, templates, merge fields, proof of delivery'; ownership.json gives template and merge_field to P6.
proposed: Read the catalogue only through the owner's answer and never as a table; this slice supplies its own treatment values and its preconditions name P6 as the owner of the template version and its Legal approval.

title: The treatment-side matching read, the shortfall columns, the breach decision code and the plan-check cadence are not specified
source: Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5, RWB E2 027 Payment matching rules with the data team v2; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1, slides 14, 15 and 18; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1, slides 18, 42 and 44; Recovery Workbench TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2, T3.1, T3.2 and T4
description: Legacy RWB-E2-027 gives the treatment side nothing more than the in-process call TreatmentApi.recordInstallmentPaid(treatmentId, proceedsId, dueDate, amount, shortfall) and the sentence that a partial match holds the shortfall on the plan. No source names the operation and the payload of the matching read that replaces that call across the service boundary; none says which treatment column carries the plan state or which carries the closed value; none gives the decision code of a plan-breach record; and none gives the cadence of the plan check beyond the 30-day cure period the design shows for R-RES-27. The story therefore records the operation name and payload as the baseline's own, writes the state on the standard state column with the outcome on DF-TRT-013 and DF-TRT-014, records the breach as the rule ID and package version of the fired row, and uses one durable timer per plan whose period is the 30 days of the design.
evidence: Legacy section 12 publishes only RuleEvaluator.evaluate, RuleCatalog.row, DecisionLogApi.write and void TreatmentApi.recordInstallmentPaid(UUID treatmentId, UUID proceedsId, LocalDate dueDate, BigDecimal amount, BigDecimal shortfall), and its section 13 adds no table on the treatment side. TSD S2 T3.1 lists DF-TRT-032, DF-TRT-033, DF-TRT-013 and DF-TRT-014 without a plan-state column. Temporal and Drools Design slide 14 shows the cure period as a durable timer of 30 days and names no other cadence; Architecture v5 slide 44 retires JOB-05 as durable timers.
area: Contract, data and workflow design of the treatment-side payment consequence
owner_role: Solution architect with the rwb-treatment and rwb-payment squads
proposed: Take the matching read from RWB-P8-E2027-CON as published, write the plan state on the standard state column with outcome BROKEN and outcome_at on a breach, stamp the rule ID and package version on the local decision record, and keep the plan check as one durable timer of the workflow with the design's 30-day cure period.

title: PAYMENT_MATCH is the rwb-payment matching package while this slice evaluates it for the plan breach on the treatment side
source: Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5, RWB E2 027 Payment matching rules with the data team v2, sections 1, 2 and 13; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1, slides 15 and 18; Recovery Workbench TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2, T4; sibling stories RWB-S2-E3001-APP and RWB-S2-E3004-APP, sections 12.3 and 19
description: Two sources place the plan consequence in two different packages. The legacy story makes PAYMENT_MATCH the package that decides the match, with the match type, the tolerance, the window, the grace and the partial floor as its row columns, and it names the package as rwb-payment's capability with JOB-07. The Temporal and Drools design keeps PAYMENT_MATCH as a Phase 1 package of S2 (slide 15) and gives the treatment route its breach rows R-RES-25, R-RES-27, R-RES-29, R-RES-30 and R-RES-31 under RESTRUCTURE (slide 18), so the plan-breach rows the treatment side needs are RESTRUCTURE rows and not PAYMENT_MATCH rows. The sibling stories of this epic place the TreatmentClosed event with RWB-S2-E3004-APP and with the closure story, which this slice is for a breached plan. This story evaluates the package the legacy key names and closes the plan on the breach outcome, keeps the package rows with rwb-decision, and publishes TreatmentClosed once.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-027 section 2 and BR10 put the tolerance, window, grace and partial floor in PAYMENT_MATCH rows and call JOB-07 in rwb-payment; Temporal and Drools Design slide 15 lists PAYMENT_MATCH among the Phase 1 packages and slide 18 puts breaks versus max_breaks under RESTRUCTURE in rwb-treatment with the note that PAYMENT_MATCH replaces payment_match_rule (T10); RWB-S2-E3001-APP section 19 and RWB-S2-E3004-APP section 12.3 leave TreatmentClosed to the plan and closure stories.
area: Rule package ownership and event ownership between P8, P7 and S2
owner_role: Solution architect with rwb-decision, rwb-payment and rwb-treatment
proposed: Keep the package, its rows and its versions with rwb-decision (P7); keep the match and the proceeds row with rwb-payment (P8); let rwb-treatment evaluate the version in force for the plan consequence the treatment row needs, take the breach threshold from the row outputs, and publish rwb.treatment.TreatmentClosed.v1 once for a breached plan, leaving the completed-plan closure to the plan story.

title: The treatment-side use of the suggestion is unspecified: the agent-run operation and its payload on the caller side, the treatment columns that hold the proposal and the model, prompt and policy versions, the 60 s wait and its fallback contract, and the decision code of a suggestion record
source: Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5, RWB E2 032 TDR offer suggestion model through the model gateway E3e v1, sections 1-19; Recovery Workbench TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2, T3.0, T3.1, T3.2, T4, T5.2 and T6.1; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1, slides 16, 18, 41 and 44; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1, slides 12, 13, 27 and 28; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4, R-UNI-32, R-UNI-39 and R-UNI-40
description: The legacy key describes the agent side end to end and gives the treatment side one in-process call: ModelSuggestionClient.suggestOffer(caseId, treatmentId) returns an OfferSuggestion and the treatment record shows it. No source states the treatment side of that seam in the target. Four things are open. One: the operation the treatment service calls and the payload it sends are not named; the legacy client takes the case ID and the treatment ID, while this slice must send the route, the band and the plan terms as well, and RWB-P10-E2032-CON fixes the answer but leaves the request beyond its three members to that contract. Two: TSD S2 T3.1 gives treatment no column for a suggestion, no column for a model code or model version, none for a prompt version and none for a policy version, and no source says whether the proposal is a column set of the treatment row, a second row or a table of its own; the prompt version in particular is required by REQ-DRI-001 and is carried by no member of the eight-member answer. Three: the 60 seconds of R-UNI-32 and of Architecture v5 slide 16 is named as a workflow wait, while DP-11 fixes a 2 s client budget on every REST hop, and no source reconciles the two waits for this hop. Four: the decision code of a suggestion record is given as D5 by the legacy section 12, but the decision codes of an override and of a fallback record are not published anywhere. The story therefore reads the operation as the one of RWB-P10-E2032-CON with the facts of the treatment added to its request, adds the proposal columns to the treatment row, carries the prompt version with the proposal from the answer or the run the answer names, declares both waits with the rule fallback on either breach, and records the override and the fallback under decision D5 with the rule ID and the package version in place of the model version.
evidence: Legacy section 12 publishes only the Java interface Optional<OfferSuggestion> suggestOffer(UUID caseId, UUID treatmentId) throws DecisionNotRecordedException, with the eight members agentRunId, decisionLogEntryId, modelCode, modelVersion, installments, monthlyAmountThb, interestRate and confidence, and section 11 writes agent_policy and agent_run fields as P3's. TSD S2 T3.1 lists DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-033 and none of them is a suggestion, a model version, a prompt version or a policy version; T3.2 lists LOV-PROPOSER, LOV-TREATMENT and LOV-TRT-OUTCOME only. Architecture v5 slide 16 gives rwb-agent the Temporal line 'AgentRunWorkflow: 60 s, then rule result' and no caller-side detail. Temporal and Drools Design slide 27 carries the note 'AI agent slow: after 60 s the rule result is used (R-UNI-32)' and slide 12 names the kit template 'Agent run with rule fallback' without its interface. DP-11 of the Template and Rules fixes one hop and a 2 s timeout on a published interface. R-UNI-32 carries the 60 seconds in its SLA column and RESUME_STATE as its target state; R-UNI-39 and R-UNI-40 carry the record and duplicate rules. RWB-P10-E2032-CON section 12.4 fixes the eight answer members and the refusal codes and leaves the request beyond case ID, treatment ID and TDR_OFFER:<treatmentId> open.
area: Service boundary, contract and data model of rwb-treatment
proposed: Fix the caller-side operation, the request members and the proposal columns with the owners of RWB-P10-E2032-CON and of the treatment entity in the wave 2 contract review, and record the decision codes of an override and of a fallback with rwb-decision before the story's Done.

title: Architecture v5 slide 16 publishes no inbound suggestion operation on rwb-agent, while the legacy treatment flow calls one synchronously
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1, slides 16, 41 and 43; Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5, RWB E2 032 TDR offer suggestion model through the model gateway E3e v1, sections 4, 12 and 13; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1, slide 12; RWB-P10-E2032-CON, sections 12.1 and 12.2
description: The two sources disagree on how a suggestion is obtained. Architecture v5 slide 16, the highest source in the R-PREC order, gives rwb-agent two inbound REST reads only - GET /agent-runs/{id} and GET/POST /agent-policies for administration - with the Temporal line 'AgentRunWorkflow: 60 s, then rule result' and the event AgentRunCompleted on the way out; no inbound operation produces a suggestion. The legacy key of the same capability has the treatment service call ModelSuggestionClient.suggestOffer in process and receive the suggestion in the same thread (sections 4 and 12), which is a synchronous answer and not a read of a run. The target therefore needs an inbound operation that slide 16 does not list. This story consumes that operation as RWB-P10-E2032-CON publishes it, on the base /api/recovery/agent/v1 with one hop and the client budget of DP-11, and treats its publication as an addition to the slide 16 list rather than a contradiction of its ownership: rwb-agent still owns the run, the prompt, the guardrail and the evaluation, and the treatment side still asks one question and waits for one answer. The placement of the answer on the treatment record - SCR-15 in this story against SCR-14 in the legacy section 15 - follows the FSD S2 screen list and is recorded with ASM-B-S2-06-E2032-6.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 16 reads 'IN: REST GET /agent-runs/{id}; GET/POST /agent-policies (admin) | events DocumentStored (intake); CaseCreated (screening) | Temporal AgentRunWorkflow: 60 s, then rule result; Tool gateway: read-only calls for the agent' and 'OUT: ... topic rwb.agent.events.v1: AgentRunCompleted'. Slide 43 lists AgentRunCompleted as event 28 produced by rwb-agent for rwb-decision, rwb-document and rwb-deviation, and does not list rwb-treatment. Legacy section 12 publishes 'public interface ModelSuggestionClient { Optional<OfferSuggestion> suggestOffer(UUID caseId, UUID treatmentId) throws DecisionNotRecordedException; }' and its section 4 step 2 has the P3 treatment service call it; section 15 puts the suggestion area on SCR-14. RWB-P10-E2032-CON section 12.1 declares one provided operation on /api/recovery/agent/v1 whose path below the base is Not specified, and section 12.2 of this story consumes it.
area: Service contract boundary between rwb-treatment and rwb-agent
proposed: Record the suggestion operation of RWB-P10-E2032-CON as an addition to the rwb-agent inbound list of Architecture v5 slide 16, and take the amendment to the architecture review that owns the slide before wave 2 closes.
